method: pyte 140x45 screen over a real `claude` TUI in a pty, signed in to a Max subscription, with `open`/BROWSER shimmed. `/rate-limit-options` typed and Return pressed: the hidden command claude opens by itself when a usage limit is hit, opened by hand so no real limit was needed. Nothing was sent to the API and no option was chosen; Escape closed it.
sanitized: Verbatim. The first screen line ('uuu ▐▛███▛█Claude Code') is pyte's rendering of the banner, kept as captured.

screens.rate-limit-options.captured.txt: `What do you want to do?` - two numbered rows, cursor on row 0, `Esc to cancel` footer. The echoed `❯ /rate-limit-options` above it carries the marker with no number. While it was open, claude's sessions/<pid>.json read status `waiting`, waitingFor `dialog open`.
